what_happened: Dispatch scoped 4 READMEs for cols=files-lines wrap. Verified on a scratch copy that Expressiveness/README.md and WeakCanonical/README.md wrap cleanly (4-col header rewrite + cols=files-lines + stripped duplicate (N files) prose). But Kamp/README.md and NfMultiAnchorBridge/README.md use a single aggregated 'loose modules' row (all loose .lean files summed into one row) that no existing generator option can reproduce: rows=subdirs silently drops the row entirely (confirmed by experiment -- no INV FAIL, just gone), and rows=both expands it into 33-49 individual per-file rows, a structural rewrite far beyond a header/option change. Per NON-GOALS, reporting and stopping rather than extending the generator; recommend these two stay unwrapped under this task.

Full scratch-copy verification loop for the 2 in-scope wraps succeeded end to end on the first attempt: wrapped Expressiveness/README.md and WeakCanonical/README.md with a 4-column header (Module/Files/Lines/Description) and cols=files-lines, ran --emit-inventory, confirmed every subdirectory total rendered as a real number (no em-dash), confirmed via key-sorted diff that every description was preserved byte-for-byte except the 10 deliberately-stripped '(N files)' parentheticals, then corrupted one count, confirmed INV FAIL named exactly that file, restored via --emit-inventory (never a pathspec checkout), and confirmed the restored file byte-matched the pre-corruption state.

Research recommendation 1 says to add a literal 1 files-count cell to each LOOSE-file row before the first --emit-inventory run, but omits the subdirectory rows. render_block keys description carry-forward on len(cells) >= ncols (ncols=4 for cols=files-lines + desc=yes), so any 3-cell row -- including every subdirectory row -- has its description replaced by the TODO_DESC placeholder. Reproduced on a scratch copy: wrapping Expressiveness/README.md without padding destroyed all 15 descriptions. Plan corrects this to: pad EVERY data row to 4 cells, loose and subdirectory alike.

Exercising the generator on a scratch copy at plan time (rather than planning from the research text alone) caught a description-destroying gap before any tracked file was touched; the corrected padded procedure was then verified end-to-end on the same scratch copy, including an idempotent --emit-inventory --check pass.

All 3 phases completed exactly as planned with zero deviations in substance: both READMEs wrapped in cols=files-lines inventory blocks, all descriptions preserved, both corrupt/restore demonstrations named exactly the right file, and WeakCanonical's KTypeSummary/ jump (1 file/122 lines -> 6 files/958 lines) matched the plan's Scope Hypothesis precisely. Sibling task 817 was concurrently rewriting other READMEs on the same tree the whole time; git-commit-phase.sh's per-phase scoped staging kept every commit limited to this task's own two files with zero scope excursions.

Phase 3 declared Verification Tier: full and named bash .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh as a criterion, but that script's gates (1-23) are entirely about .claude/ deploy-tree consistency (hooks, extension merges, orphan detection, shellcheck lint, etc.) and none maps to a README-content edit under FormalSystem/. Neither run-all.sh --only (discovers shell test suites only) nor verify-deploy.sh --only-gate N expresses the two checks that actually cover this edit class (check-module-invariants.sh --emit-inventory --check, readme-lint.sh). Resolved per the dispatch's own UNMAPPABLE CRITERION guidance: ran both named checks directly and deferred the full verify-deploy.sh gate to the batch-level run, recording the discharge in the plan's phase-3 task list and the task summary.
